gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Dreamy and spaced way out, Starborn scatters its letters across the line with a dark stripe of lowercase running through. Noto Sans Khmer takes the opposite job, with generous notches in its curves and small letters that stand almost capital-tall.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Noto Sans Khojki reads open and light, with wide exits that let light through and a big, clear eye on every e. Starborn sits above it, all drifting gaps and one dark lowercase stripe.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-khudawa: Noto Sans Khudawadi reads friendly and level, its capitals barely taller than the lowercase and its rounds left unlatched. Starborn's wide-spaced heading floats above, so a long page would feel gentle.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-kr: Noto Sans KR reads sturdy and generous, with open gaps in its curves and short stems beside a big x-height. Starborn drifts above it, spaced wide and dark, giving the page two speeds.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-lao: Contemporary and tall-bodied, Noto Sans Lao pushes its x-height well past the usual while keeping every mouth open on c, e and a. Starborn's dreamy, widely spaced heading is the sharper half of the pair.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-lao-loo: Wide gaps, dark stripe. Starborn has a hazy, ethereal look, while the words below hold together as solid blocks. Noto Sans Lao Looped does the quiet work, with bowls left unfinished on one side, where Starborn does the dreaming.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Starborn spreads its ethereal letters far apart, with a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through each line. And Noto Sans Lepcha answers its drift with wide-open curves and a lowercase as tall as cast iron capitals.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Dreamy gaps and a heavy lowercase stripe: that is Starborn, a heading that floats more than it sits. But Noto Sans Limbu keeps the text grounded, its gaping curves and tall small letters making a long page easy going.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Ethereal is the first word for Starborn, whose letters sit far apart under a thick, dark lowercase stripe, with Noto Sans Lisu tucked beneath. Their strongest quality is the gap between a dreamy heading and wide-open, businesslike text.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Noto Sans Lydian reads soft and unfussy, its capitals barely taller than lowercase and its openings wide as a sprung paper clip. And Starborn gives it a dreamy, widely spaced heading with a dark stripe of lowercase.
